title: Part-time work and study balance
description: A job can fund student life and build experience — as long as it does not quietly eat the degree.

body.heading: Protect study first
paragraphs: The course is the investment; the job supports it. Decide your maximum weekly work hours before job hunting, and be honest about deadlines and exam periods when term gets intense.
Many students find that a modest, steady number of hours beats intense bursts that collide with assignments. Consistency protects both your grades and your energy.

body.heading: Choose work that gives more
paragraphs: Campus jobs, tutoring, and roles related to your subject can pay in experience as well as money. Even unrelated work builds reliability, teamwork, and references.

Check the rules that apply to you: your course, visa, or funding may limit hours, and your employer should follow local rules on pay and breaks. If something feels off, your student advice service can help you check.

body.heading: Budget the wages, rest properly
paragraphs: Give part-time wages a simple plan — essentials, a little saving, guilt-free fun — and protect sleep like it is part of the job. Tired students earn less and learn less.

takeaway: Set your maximum work hours first, choose steady work, and protect study and sleep.
